name: Maison à Bordeaux
features: Three stacked houses; a 3 x 3.5 m lift platform moves through all levels for the wheelchair-using owner.
note: Two Flickr photos by Ann Chou (1600x1200 and 1200x1600), in Category:Buildings by Rem Koolhaas and Houses in Bordeaux; descriptions name the house. No dedicated Commons category.

name: Bibliothèque Alexis de Tocqueville
features: Cross-shaped plan whose four glazed wings point to landmarks of Caen, around a central reading hall.
note: Several interior CC0 photos too.

name: Tours Aillaud (Tours Nuages)
features: Rounded towers up to 38 floors, covered in cloud-pattern mosaic and pierced by round and drop-shaped windows.

photos.file: File:Tours Aillaud, de la prefecture des Hauts de Seine.JPG

name: Choux de Créteil
features: Ten round towers whose balconies are curved concrete petals, like the leaves of a cabbage.
note: 33 files in the category.

name: Les Arcades du Lac
features: Social housing as a classical garden city: precast concrete arcades and blocks laid out on axes by a lake.
note: 27 files in the category.

name: Antigone
features: A one-kilometre classical axis of squares and precast housing blocks running from the old town to the river Lez.

photos.file: File:Montpellier. Antigone disctrict (1978-2000) Ricardo Bofill, architect (15201294644).jpg
File:Montpellier - Antigone - Place de Théssalie - Designed by Riccardo Bofill.jpg

name: Étoiles d'Ivry
features: Star-shaped concrete housing of triangular terraces, each flat with its own planted garden on a neighbour's roof.

photos.file: File:Etoiles d'Ivry @ Brutalist housing project @ Jean Renaudie @ Ivry-sur-Seine (30581493681).jpg
File:Etoiles d'Ivry @ Brutalist housing project @ Jean Renaudie @ Ivry-sur-Seine (30669358255).jpg

note: About 30 Flickr photos (5472x3648, CC BY 2.0); no dedicated category found.

name: Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport Terminal 1
features: Round concrete drum crossed by glass-tube escalators, linked by tunnels to seven satellite gates.
note: 54 files in the category.

name: Palais Bulles
features: A cluster of concrete bubbles with round windows spilling down the red rocks above the bay of Cannes.

photos.file: File:PHOTO PALAIS BULLES Théoule-sur-Mer ANTTILOVAG ARCHITECTURE DESIGN ORGANICARCHITECTURE HABITOLOGUE 1989 1.jpg

note: The 3264x4928 file is the lead image of the Wikipedia articles; its description doesn't say interior or exterior, so check before use. Palais-bulle-gil-zetbase.jpg (1500x1001) is the big salon window.

name: Ricola Europe Production and Storage Building
features: Long walls of polycarbonate panels screen-printed with a repeated leaf photo; rain streams down the end walls.

photos.file: File:Ricola-Europe SA Production and Storage Building (3497748038).jpg

note: One Flickr photo, 2592x1944.

name: Hoenheim-Nord Tram Terminus
features: Tilted concrete canopy and car park whose white lines and light strips follow the movement of cars and trams.

photos.file: File:Strasbourg, Tramway, Endstation Hoenheim Gare von Zaha Hadid 6.jpg
File:Strasbourg, Tramway, Endstation Hoenheim Gare von Zaha Hadid 12.jpg

name: Lascaux IV
features: A long low building cut into the hillside like a fault line, where visitors walk into a replica of the cave.
note: Series Lascaux-IV 01-30 (4288x2848, public domain); check which show the outside.

name: Villa Méditerranée
features: Its upper floor cantilevers 40 m over a pool of sea water, with a conference hall sunk below it.
note: 1751x1179 Flickr photo.

name: Cité de l'Océan et du Surf
by: Steven Holl Architects with Solange Fabião
features: The roof is a concave public square, 'under the sky', with two glass 'boulders' sitting on it.
note: One general view, 4096x3072.

name: IBM Research Centre, La Gaude
features: Y-shaped wings raised on sculpted concrete piers, with deep precast window frames.

name: Le Fresnoy
features: A great roof over the old 1920s leisure halls; the 'in-between' space under it holds catwalks and stairs.

name: Orange Cube
features: Orange perforated metal cube by the Saône, hollowed by a huge conical void for light and views.

photos.file: File:Lyon - Fourvière et le cube orange (18082025358).jpg

name: Rue des Suisses Housing
features: Street fronts behind folding metal shutters; in the garden, low blocks wrapped in rolling wooden blinds.

photos.file: File:L'immeuble Herzog & de Meuron de la rue des Suisses, Paris 2007.jpg

note: One photo, 2592x3872.

name: FRAC Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur
features: Skin of hundreds of tilted, white-enamelled glass panels that break the facade up like pixels.
note: Four Flickr photos, 2013.

name: LUMA Arles Tower
features: A 56 m tower of stacked stainless-steel boxes twisting up from a glass drum that echoes the Roman arena.
note: 2048x2048 photos titled in Hebrew 'overall view' and 'street view'; check they show the tower clearly. Category:Tour Luma also has 2016-2022 town views where the tower is small.

name: Musée Jean Cocteau, Séverin Wunderman Collection
features: A low white box on the seafront, its glass walls behind a fringe of irregular dark concrete fins.

photos.file: File:Le musée Jean Cocteau, collection S. Wunderman (Menton, France) (40635031623).jpg

note: Category also holds the old Bastion museum; use the files named above.

name: Musée départemental Arles antique
features: Triangular plan clad in bright blue enamelled glass, set beside the remains of the Roman circus.

name: Historial de la Grande Guerre
features: White concrete galleries added behind the medieval castle of Péronne, looking over a pond.
commons_category: Category:Historial de la Grande Guerre in Péronne (Somme)
note: Only CAM Historial.jpg (2888x2200, rear view over the pond) shows Ciriani's building; the other exterior files show the castle.

name: Fondation Avicenne (Maison de l'Iran)
by: Claude Parent, André Bloc, Mohsen Foroughi, Heydar Ghiai
features: Student rooms in blocks hung from giant steel portal frames, lifted clear of the ground.

photos.file: File:Montrouge 92120 Boulevard Romain Rolland towards Fondation Avicienne.jpg

note: Both files are in the building's category, but one looks down a boulevard towards it and the other is a general view of the south of the Cité; check how large the building is in frame. If neither is good enough it is a strong drawing candidate.

name: UNESCO Headquarters
by: Marcel Breuer, Pier Luigi Nervi, Bernard Zehrfuss
features: Y-shaped Secretariat on sculpted concrete pilotis, beside a conference hall with a folded concrete roof.

photos.file: File:Architecture, Paris UNESCO House - UNESCO - PHOTO0000002877 0000.tiff

note: Category holds 177 files, mostly UNESCO archive scans (CC BY-SA 3.0 IGO). The named file shows the Avenue de Suffren entrance with the Secretariat on the right; exact file title abbreviated by the API summary, check it.

name: Maison de la Radio
features: A ring of offices nearly 500 m round, with a tall archive tower at its centre, on the bank of the Seine.

photos.file: File:Radio France @ Ile aux Cygnes @ Paris (41147366065).jpg

note: Exact file names were abbreviated by the API summary; look them up in the category.

name: Les Orgues de Flandre
features: Housing towers that step up and down like organ pipes, named after musical forms.

photos.file: File:Orgues Flandre vus depuis Belvédère Buttes Chaumont Paris 1.jpg

name: Villa dall'Ava
features: Two boxes on thin, randomly tilted columns, with a rooftop pool aimed at the Eiffel Tower.
note: The 3024x3024 file's description reads only 'Haus Boudet', so check it shows the villa; Villa dall'Ava.jpg is 779x1000 (passes the 800px rule).

name: Pavillon Noir
features: A dance centre in a glass box held by a black concrete exoskeleton of slanting struts.
note: Found by a search for Pavillon Noir Aix Ricciotti (2048x1356). Category:Pavillon Noir is an unrelated festival stage.

name: CMA CGM Tower
features: A 147 m glass tower whose curved lines sweep down and split apart at its base by the port.

photos.file: File:Coastal panorama with CMA CGM tower Marseille 2026.JPG

note: Only one free file (5660x4240), a coastal panorama naming the tower; check it is large enough in frame. If not, this is a drawing candidate.

name: Fondation Jérôme Seydoux-Pathé
features: A curved shell of perforated aluminium rising in a courtyard behind a facade carved by Rodin.
note: Descriptions don't say whether they show the shell or the street facade; check.

name: Musée de la Romanité
features: A rippling 'toga' of thousands of glass squares, facing the Roman amphitheatre across a square.

photos.file: File:Musée de la Romanité de Nîmes.jpeg
File:Jardin du Musée de la Romanité.jpg

note: The first file's description is just a date; check it shows the facade.

name: Le Volcan
features: A white truncated cone and a smaller one rise from a sunken public square.
